newsitem.title: CROATIA: World Bank postpones loans for Serb-held enclave.
newsitem.headline: World Bank postpones loans for Serb-held enclave.

text.p: The World Bank has postponed two $100 million loans for the reconstruction of Croatia's last Serb-held enclave pending the successful completion of its peaceful return to Zagreb rule, officials said on Tuesday.

"We first want to see the efficient implementation of the (peace) agreement so that the programme could get underway as soon as possible," Susan Louise Rutledge, World Bank representative at talks in Zagreb, told HINA news agency .
Croatian deputy prime minister Ivica Kostovic said the first loan should have been granted "very soonish", but is now tied to the holding of local elections in the enclave of Eastern Slavonia.
The loans should be used for the area's economic recovery, the removal of land mines and the reconstruction of the war-shattered infrastructure, HINA said.

Eastern Slavonia, now under interim U.N. control, is to be fully reintegrated into Croatia by the end of 1997. Elections of local administration should be not later than one month before the end of the U.N. mandate there. The mandate, which expires in January, will be extended either for another six or 12 months.
